method: I drew the cars, road and thought bubbles and used HTML and CSS to create an animation. I changed the viewpoint and adjusted the movement and timing to show how one driver’s response affects the cars behind. The sequence uses planned keyframes.
related_work: Reynolds’ Boids model showed me how complex flock behaviour can emerge from simple local rules, which connected with my interest in traditional beliefs and leaf divination. Wiener’s Cybernetics introduced me to the role of information and feedback in control systems. Sugiyama and his colleagues demonstrated that traffic jams can arise even without a bottleneck, revealing how local interactions generate collective patterns.
conclusion_future_work: The project helped me connect several ideas from the course. Divination raised questions about interpretation, while datafication made me consider what could be recorded and checked. The traffic animation gave me a way to explore feedback and collective patterns.
results_discussion: The class discussion about observing and analysing birds first made me interested in prediction. I connected this with traditional beliefs about animals sensing environmental changes and with leaf divination in Chinese culture. I considered creating a website about predicting disasters through animal behaviour.However, datafication raised practical questions. How could I record animal behaviour as useful data? How could I check whether a behaviour was connected to an environmental change? I had limited access to animals, and disasters happen infrequently, so gathering enough observations would be difficult.I then moved from bird flocks to traffic jams. Both made me think about individuals responding to those around them. My early animation used a circular road, but I found the relationship between the movement and the theories unclear. I changed to a side-on view and emailed my tutor for advice.He suggested considering first order, second order and third order cybernetics. After further discussion, I focused on first-order cybernetics. The driver observes the gap, adjusts their speed and then responds to the changed gap. Thought bubbles make this feedback process visible.The wider view shows drivers slowing down one after another, even after the first car has moved on. This expresses emergent complexity through many local responses. It also connects with decentralisation, as each driver responds to nearby cars and no single driver directs the whole queue.
title: week 3
introduction: This week, we explored divination, datafication, cybernetics, emergent complexity and decentralisation. These topics made me think about how people interpret signs, turn observations into data and understand patterns. My project began with an idea about animal behaviour and prediction, then developed into a traffic jam animation exploring individual responses and collective behaviour.
